title: Buddy rebuild — round 2: smaller cards, quieter replies, more button options

steps.path: When Claude asks you a multiple-choice question
steps.headline: The question card now shows one question at a time, with small choices you tap, and fits without scrolling.
steps.changed: Choices are small chips that wrap; each one's explanation shows when you point at it. The note box hides behind "+ Note" (picking Other opens it). With several questions it says 1/2, and picking an answer moves to the next one.
steps.measured: About 160 px tall for a two-question card, against more than 480 px (taller than the window) in round 1
steps.notice: You answer from the buddy without scrolling. Same answers reach Claude as from the main window's card.
steps.risk: Explanations are hidden until you point at a choice.

steps.path: When a session gets stuck or its provider stalls
steps.headline: The warning box is tighter: smaller padding and text, buttons under the sentence.
steps.changed: Less padding inside the box and slightly smaller words, so a short warning stays two lines.
steps.notice: Warnings take less of the window and still have their buttons.

steps.path: Every message in the buddy chat
steps.headline: Dates and times show only on the last message; on any other, point at it for a moment to see its time.
steps.changed: Times are folded away except on the newest message, and appear after the pointer rests on a message for about half a second. The tool steps and file cards in this picture use the slim style from the next question.
steps.notice: Less clutter between messages; the newest message still says when it arrived.
steps.risk: Checking an older message's time takes a short hover instead of a glance.

steps.path: Inside Claude's replies in the buddy
steps.headline: How much room should a reply's tool steps and file cards take in the buddy?
steps.notice: Only the buddy changes; the main window keeps its full cards. Questions and permission requests always show in full whichever you pick.

variants.label: Slim lines
variants.summary: Each step group and file card is one plain line with no box around it; press it to open the details as before.
variants.risk: Still one line per kind of thing a reply did.

variants.label: One summary line
variants.summary: Everything a reply did beyond its words becomes one quiet line, such as "1 step · 1 file"; press it to see the cards.
variants.risk: Files Claude sent you are one press away instead of visible.

variants.label: Words only
variants.summary: Only what Claude says. Steps and files are not shown in the buddy at all; you see them in the main window.
variants.risk: A file Claude sent you is not reachable from the buddy.

steps.path: The buddy and his chat on your desktop
steps.headline: Four more places for the buddy's actions (screenshot, bigger or smaller window, open YouCoded, hide). Which one?
steps.notice: Every option now includes the new size button (two diagonal arrows, "Bigger window"). Every option except Toolbar removes the separate round-button window, so dragging him has one less window to keep in step.

variants.label: One ⋯ menu
variants.summary: One small "⋯" at the right of the top row holds all four actions (shown open).
variants.risk: Screenshot takes two presses instead of one.

variants.label: Right-click him
variants.summary: Screenshot sits by Attach and the size button in the top row; right-clicking the buddy himself gives Open YouCoded and Hide (shown open).
variants.risk: Right-click is hidden until you know about it; a touchscreen needs a long press.

variants.label: Appear on hover
variants.summary: The four icons appear in the top row only while your pointer is over it (shown pointed at); the rest of the time the session name keeps the full width.
variants.risk: Nothing hints the icons are there until you point at the top row; no hover on a touchscreen.

variants.label: Labelled toolbar
variants.summary: A thin row of small labelled buttons under the message box: Screenshot, Bigger, Open app, Hide.
variants.risk: Costs about 24 px of height in every chat.

steps.headline: The size button switches the chat to this larger window and back, and remembers your choice.
steps.changed: The button is the two diagonal arrows; where it sits follows your pick above. The conversation rows Claude names in a reply lost their outer frame.
steps.notice: Room for long replies and code when you want it; the small size the rest of the time.
steps.risk: On a small laptop screen the large size covers more of what is behind it.
